input.cptMissing: Select a CPT from the project.
input.recordHint: Can be left empty: you then see only the expected blow count. Pasting from a spreadsheet also works: two columns (depth, blows), one interval per row.

visual.empty: Select a CPT and a depth range to show the expected blow count.
visual.aria: Expected and counted blows per interval against depth, with the cone resistance

sheet.title: Driving record assessment
sheet.pass: The driving record matches the CPT
sheet.failText: The driving record deviates from the CPT
sheet.m1: The formula is a rule of thumb from practice: the work needed to push the area D² over one interval against the cone resistance, divided by the energy per blow. It is not a formula from a standard.
sheet.m2: This is not a bearing capacity calculation. The bearing capacity follows from the CPTs in accordance with NEN 9997-1.
sheet.m3: A difference of up to about 50 % between expected and counted is normal. Look mainly at the trend with depth: the blow count should rise where the cone resistance rises.
sheet.m4: qc is the average of the CPT over the interval. Hammer efficiency, shaft friction and the distance to the CPT are not included in the formula.

errors.noCpt: Select a CPT; the expected blow count follows from the cone resistance.
errors.hammer: Enter the ram mass and the drop height of the pile hammer.
errors.pile: Enter the size of the pile.
errors.tocht: The interval length must be greater than 0.
errors.tolerance: The allowed deviation must be greater than 0.
errors.range: The range must run from a smaller to a larger depth.
errors.blows: Every counted interval has at least one blow.

warn.beyondCpt: The CPT reaches {{depth}} m; there is no expectation below that.
warn.noQc: The CPT has no readings for part of the counted intervals.
warn.higher: On average {{pct}} % more blows were counted than expected: harder ground than at the CPT, a lower hammer efficiency or a different drop height.
warn.lower: On average {{pct}} % fewer blows were counted than expected: softer ground than at the CPT or a heavier hammer than entered.
